title: Drupal Commerce Core unauthenticated access bypass exploited in the wild (SA-CONTRIB-2026-254, Highly critical 21/25); not in CISA KEV
why: Drupal's advisory SA-CONTRIB-2026-254 (Oct 28) states the flaw is actively exploited in the wild; covered by BleepingComputer, The Hacker News and SecurityWeek on Oct 30. Ostorlab and Rescana report it is not in CISA KEV (catalog 2026.10.29, checked Oct 30). NVD has no score yet. Not a Microsoft product; no KEV entry. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 1: the collector's CISA KEV feed shows no additions since the Oct 30 Ivanti entries, so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 2: collector's CISA KEV feed shows no additions since the last run and Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (Oct 31) does not include it, so still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade Commerce Core to 3.3.13 (or 8.x-2.41) now, then audit recent orders for unpaid, re-priced or unexpectedly adjusted orders as Drupal advises.
product: Drupal Commerce Core 3.x before 3.3.13 and 8.x-2.x before 8.x-2.41

title: Trojanized Claude Code VS Code extension 2.1.313 on Cursor marketplace / Open VSX planted persistent SSH backdoor (up to 5,000 users)
why: Cursor's security notice (Oct 29) confirms a malicious 2.1.313 build was served for ~11 hours to at most 5,000 users; analysis by OpenSourceMalware (OTX pulse), StepSecurity and Phorion, reported by BleepingComputer, THN and oss-security on Oct 30. Supply-chain compromise with no CVE, so no KEV entry; no Microsoft advisory or Defender guidance seen. Microsoft's own VS Code Marketplace was not reported to serve the bad build. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 1: the collector's CISA KEV feed shows no additions since the Oct 30 Ivanti entries, so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 2: collector's CISA KEV feed shows no additions since the last run and Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (Oct 31) does not include it, so still not in KEV.
action: Find any endpoint that ran anthropic.claude-code 2.1.313, run Cursor's published check/remediation scripts, remove the unauthorized SSH key and persistence, and rotate credentials reachable from those hosts.
product: Anthropic.claude-code VS Code extension 2.1.313 installed from the Cursor extension marketplace / Open VSX on Oct 29, 2026 (2.1.312 and 2.1.314 clean)

title: WordPress Core unauthenticated RCE race during core upgrades (CVE-2026-119977): ~63,000 exploitation attempts in 24h; not in CISA KEV
why: Wordfence telemetry shows active exploitation attempts (62,969 blocked in 24h) polling wp-content/upgrade staging paths since the Oct 28 fix; Ostorlab and Rescana (Oct 31) confirm attempts only, no confirmed compromise, and not in CISA KEV (catalog 2026.10.30). The collector's KEV feed shows no additions since. Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Nov 2: collector's CISA KEV feed shows no additions since the last run and Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (Oct 31) does not include it, so still not in KEV.
action: Confirm every WordPress site is on 7.1.4 (or its branch backport), deny web access to wp-content/upgrade/ at the web server, and hunt logs for requests to PHP files under wp-content/upgrade.
product: WordPress Core 4.7 through 7.1.3 (fixed in 7.1.4 and backported branch releases)

title: GitLab CI regex (Ruby Onigmo) unauthenticated RCE, CVSS 10 (KEV): Alpine Linux rebuilds its GitLab after near-successful exploitation; GitLab installs on their own Ruby stay vulnerable after upgrading
why: In CISA KEV (added Oct 29), so Microsoft/Defender already has the public signal. New this run: Alpine Linux's incident report (BleepingComputer Nov 1, THN) shows an attacker tuning the exploit to its custom GitLab image Oct 20-21, with 4 of 8 worker crashes getting partway through the exploit.
action: Confirm every GitLab server runs the latest branch release AND a fixed Ruby (3.3.13/3.4.12/4.0.9+) if not using GitLab's Omnibus/official images; re-pull alpinelinux/gitlab:19.3.6 if pulled before Oct 27; hunt for repeated worker crashes on CI config parsing.
product: GitLab CE/EE before the Oct 12/21 security releases (e.g. 19.3.4 and older on the 19.3 branch); self-compiled or custom-image GitLab on Ruby older than 3.3.13 / 3.4.12 / 4.0.9

title: Synology DSM NAS hit by C3RB3R (Cerber) ransomware via unauthenticated DSM flaws; Synology confirms exploitation, not in CISA KEV
why: Synology's Oct 29 notice confirms threat actors are exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024 (it points to SA-24:20, CVE-2024-10441) to encrypt outdated DSM devices. Qihoo 360's Oct 29 incident analysis attributes the cases it examined to unauthenticated CVE-2026-13639/13684 (SA-26:13, Sep 18) instead, so which flaw is used is disputed. BleepingComputer (Nov 2) reports a wave of victims; Shadowserver tracks 380k+ exposed Synology NAS. Missing on Microsoft's side: none of the three CVEs appears in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed shows no Synology additions; pentest-tools lists CVE-2024-10441 as not in KEV, undated). Not a Microsoft product.
action: Update every Synology NAS to the latest DSM build for its branch (at least 7.4-90075 / 7.3.2-86009-4 / 7.2.2-72806-9 / 7.2.1-69057-12), take DSM management ports off the internet, and search shares for .L0CK3D files and read-me3.txt.

title: Langflow OSS unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2026-110186) and auth bypass (CVE-2026-93680, public Metasploit module) through 1.12.8; fixed only in 1.13.0
why: IBM's bulletin (Oct 28, updated Oct 29) covers unauthenticated RCE CVE-2026-110186 and auth bypass CVE-2026-93680 in every Langflow release through 1.12.8. The Hacker News and GBHackers covered it Nov 2: a public Metasploit module already cites CVE-2026-93680 (it opens an MCP session without credentials and lists tools, but does not run code), the only fix is 1.13.0, and there is no workaround. Missing on Microsoft's side: neither flaw is in CISA KEV as of the Oct 30 catalog update (the collector's KEV feed shows no additions since). No in-the-wild exploitation reported. Not a Microsoft product.
action: Upgrade Langflow to 1.13.0 (set LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD first; auto-login is disabled), keep Langflow behind an authenticating proxy, and rotate API keys stored in flows.
product: Langflow OSS 1.0.0 through 1.12.8 (PyPI langflow, langflowai/langflow Docker); fixed in 1.13.0

title: Gotenberg unauthenticated RCE (ExifTool metadata-key injection, CVSS 9.8) exploited in the wild by multiple actors; not in CISA KEV
why: VulnCheck canaries recorded 1,358 exploitation events from 128 source IPs over 30 days, including an actor dropping a custom Go reverse shell (cache_base) in early October (VulnCheck blog, analysis Oct 24; THN ThreatsDay Oct 29); a separate cryptomining campaign is documented by The Hunter's Ledger. A public PoC and Nuclei template exist. VulnCheck notes it is NOT in CISA KEV (VulnCheck KEV since June). Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 1: the collector's CISA KEV feed shows no additions since the Oct 30 Ivanti entries, so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 2: collector's CISA KEV feed shows no additions since the last run and Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (Oct 31) does not include it, so still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade every Gotenberg container to 8.31.0 or later, keep port 3000 off untrusted networks behind an authenticating proxy, and hunt for POSTs to /forms/pdfengines/metadata/write and unexpected outbound connections from Gotenberg containers.
product: Gotenberg before 8.31.0 (/forms/pdfengines/metadata/write endpoint)

title: Supermarket refrigeration-controller sabotage spreads to Belgium and Sweden: Delhaize, Carrefour Belgium and ICA fridges driven to 50°C overnight Nov 1-2
why: New wave: NL Times (Nov 2) reports at least dozens of Delhaize stores, butcher De Laet & Van Haver and 15 Carrefour Belgium stores hit late Nov 1/early Nov 2, and Swedish media report ICA stores with cooling at 50°C overnight (HN discussion, Sweden Herald). Same pattern as the Oct 11-12 French campaign (CERT-FR CERTFR-2026-ALE-012: numerous compromised Danfoss AK-SM/AK-SC controllers). A public PoC for the Danfoss 'code of the day' auth bypass CVE-2025-41450 has been on GitHub since Oct 13. CISA's KEV file listed no Danfoss entry as of Oct 12 and none appear in KEV additions Oct 25-31; no authority has confirmed which flaw is used (the CVE link is inference). Not a Microsoft product.
action: Take every refrigeration/building controller off the public internet now (contractor access only via VPN with MFA), upgrade AK-SM 8xxA to R4.3.1+, plan replacement of EOL AK-SM 800/AK-SC 355, and check setpoints and defrost schedules against baseline.
product: Danfoss AK-SM 800A / AK-SM 8xxA System Manager before R4.3.1 (auth bypass fixed in R4.2), end-of-life AK-SM 800 and AK-SC 355; Copeland/Dixell XWEB controllers

title: Linux kernel IPv4 TCP handshake use-after-free (CVSS 9.8): Fortinet PSIRT advisory, SANS MPTCP guidance; Ubuntu still unfixed, not in KEV
why: Anthropic described an unauthenticated remote root exploit against MPTCP listeners (code not published, though one blog claims a public PoC; unconfirmed). PatchMon (Oct 30): Ubuntu lists every supported kernel as Vulnerable and Red Hat has deferred its fix; Debian, SUSE, Oracle and parts of Amazon Linux are fixed. Oct 31 oss-security post adds init_on_free=1 as an extra interim hardening option; HN chatter continues. No in-the-wild reports; not in CISA KEV (no KEV additions since Oct 30). Change Nov 1: Red Hat shipped fixed kernels for RHEL 8, 9 and 10 (Atlas Security timeline); Ubuntu's tracker still lists every release as Vulnerable (fixed packages named but unreleased); AlmaLinux fixed kernels in testing. Still not in KEV, no exploitation in the wild reported. Change Nov 2: Fortinet PSIRT published FG-IR-26-188 for this kernel RCE (CVSS 9.8) and SANS ISC posted guidance on spotting Multipath TCP use. Still not in CISA KEV (no KEV additions this run) and no in-the-wild exploitation reported.
action: Patch RHEL 8/9/10 to Red Hat's Nov 1 kernels and reboot; on Ubuntu and others still waiting, drop inbound IPv4 TCP packets with IP options (nft 'ip hdrlength gt 5' rule) and find MPTCP listeners (Go 1.24+ services use MPTCP by default). Check Fortinet FG-IR-26-188 for affected Fortinet products.

title: Hugging Face trust_remote_code malware campaign returns: fake Qwen2 models drop GPU miners, reverse shells and SSH backdoors on inference servers
why: Pluto Security found 31 malicious repos across seven Hugging Face accounts; a second wave appeared within days of takedown and a near-identical model uploaded Oct 25 was still live when BleepingComputer checked (Oct 29). Flagship model reached 28,412 downloads. No CVE; no Microsoft advisory or KEV entry applies, and the article notes HF's scanners do not analyse bundled Python code. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 1: the collector's CISA KEV feed shows no additions since the Oct 30 Ivanti entries, so still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 2: collector's CISA KEV feed shows no additions since the last run and Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (Oct 31) does not include it, so still not in KEV.
action: Disable trust_remote_code by default, allowlist model sources, and check GPU inference hosts against Pluto Security's published indicators (via the BleepingComputer article); treat any host that loaded these models as compromised and rotate its credentials.
vendor: Hugging Face Hub (abused); targets Xinference, GPUStack
product: Self-hosted inference servers loading Hub models with trust_remote_code enabled

title: Android 'SMS of Death' (CVE-2026-58882): public zero-click PoC crashes telephony and can boot-loop phones; Android 12/13 left unpatched
why: Researcher Mark Blaszczyk published a working PoC on Oct 29 (BleepingComputer, heise, Cybernews): an 8-byte malformed WAP Push SMS crashes com.android.phone, drops active calls including emergency calls, and ~20 messages can boot-loop a device. Google shipped the fix in October updates for Android 14-17 but has not yet listed it in a bulletin (expected Nov, Critical); Android 12/13 get no fix. No in-the-wild attacks reported; not in CISA KEV. Rechecked Nov 2: collector's CISA KEV feed shows no additions since the last run and Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (Oct 31) does not include it, so still not in KEV.
action: Use MDM to find managed Android devices below the October 2026 security patch level and push updates; plan replacement or restricted use for Android 12/13 devices that will not get a fix.
product: Android telephony framework (WapPushOverSms/decodeWapPdu), Android 12 through 16; fixed in October 2026 updates for Android 14-17 only

title: Northflank PaaS breach: customers told to assume all environment variables decrypted; stolen AI API keys already abused
why: Northflank's status page (Oct 30-31) confirms multiple customers saw unauthorized use of AI API keys stored on the platform and tells all customers to assume every environment variable was decrypted; Wiz raised the alert and lists Northflank among nine AI-developer-platform incidents in October (LLMJacking). Entry point and customer count undisclosed. A SaaS breach, so no KEV/MSRC entry applies. Rechecked Nov 2: collector's CISA KEV feed shows no additions since the last run and Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (Oct 31) does not include it, so still not in KEV.
action: If you use Northflank, revoke and reissue every secret stored there at the issuing provider (AI, cloud, database), disable public add-on access, and review AI-provider usage and billing logs since Oct 30.
product: Northflank cloud application platform (customer environment variables, secret groups, global secrets)

title: Barracuda Email Security Gateway pre-auth config-restore bypass (CVSS4 9.3) chains with root command injection CVE-2026-111560; fixed 9.4.0.030
why: Barracuda and Mandiant (MNDT-2026-0042/0041) disclosed on Nov 2 that an unauthenticated attacker who can reach the ESG admin interface (port 8000 by default) can restore a crafted config backup, and chained with the timezone command injection gets root. No exploitation or public PoC reported. Missing on Microsoft's side: neither CVE is in CISA KEV (HOL: not on KEV as of catalog 2026.10.30, and none of Barracuda, Mandiant or CISA reports exploitation). Barracuda ESG was mass-exploited in 2023, so it is a likely target. Not a Microsoft product.
action: Upgrade ESG to 9.4.0.030 or later (patch BNSF-40425/40430), set Firmware Patches to apply automatically, and make sure the admin interface (port 8000) is not reachable from the internet.
product: Barracuda Email Security Gateway before 9.4.0.030 (CVE-2026-116606); CVE-2026-111560 also hits Load Balancer ADC <=6.4.0, WAF <=11.0.1, Web Security Gateway <=16.1.100.100, Message Archiver <=5.5.4.0, WAF Control Center <=2.2.1

title: MathLive postMessage HTML injection: ChatGPT share-link account-takeover chain published; fixed in MathLive 0.111.2, other embedders exposed
why: Parameter published the full chain with payloads on Oct 28 (HN front page Oct 31): MathLive's top-level keyboard controller accepted postMessage layouts with HTML from any origin, which together with a YouTube JSONP CSP bypass gave JavaScript execution as chatgpt.com from a public share link. OpenAI fixed ChatGPT on Oct 26 (P1); MathLive 0.111.2 (Oct 31) changes the default origin check. No CVE, no in-the-wild use reported, not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 2: collector's CISA KEV feed shows no additions since the last run and Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (Oct 31) does not include it, so still not in KEV.

title: Apache Struts2 <=7.4.0: researcher full-discloses OGNL sandbox escape to code execution plus 6 other unfixed flaws (no CVE, no Apache advisory)
why: Seven Full Disclosure posts by Daniel Owens on Nov 1 describe unfixed Struts2 flaws, headlined by an OGNL sandbox escape: SecurityMemberAccess only checks direct calls, so an allowed call that evaluates a nested expression can reach arbitrary code; a JSON-plugin element-count limit bypass of the S2-072 hardening is also described. The latest Apache bulletins (S2-075..078, 7.4.0 on Oct 2) do not cover them, and there is no CVE, no Apache advisory and no KEV entry. Only the FD posts (and GitHub mirrors) were seen; the full post text and any PoC were not verified.
action: Inventory Struts2 apps; make sure none evaluate user input as OGNL (no forced %{} evaluation of request data), keep the OGNL allowlist enabled, cap REST request bodies at the proxy, and watch for an Apache S2 bulletin.
product: Apache Struts2 Core, REST, JSON and Spring plugins 7.4.0 and earlier (JSON issue also in 7.5.0 snapshot of Oct 28)
